$comment: PUBLISHED PAYLOADS THAT ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CONTRACT EXAMPLES. Read by payload_parity.py.
Seeded 2026-09-09 against api/mqtt/schema/iotc-rfd40-90-mqtt.asyncapi.json, info.version
THIS FILE IS PRINTED IN FULL ON EVERY RUN, and that is the whole design. An escape hatch
nobody sees is an allowlist, and an allowlist is how a gate stops meaning anything. The
check prints every entry with its reason before it prints a single finding, so waiving
something costs you a line of output on every push forever.
TWO HARD RULES FOR AN ENTRY, both enforced by --selftest:
1. The key is '<path relative to api/mqtt/prose/>:<CONST>'. Exactly one colon.
2. The reason must name either the upstream issue that retires it, or the scenario the
contract does not carry. A reason under 40 characters fails the self-test, because
'legacy' and 'known' are not reasons.
A WAIVER THAT IS NO LONGER NEEDED IS A FAILURE, not a harmless leftover. If the page or the
const stops needing it -- because a drop finally ships the example, or because the page was
rewritten -- the recorded reason has become a false statement about this repository, and the
check reports it as STALE. Delete the entry in the commit that observes it.
WHY THERE ARE MORE THAN THREE (2026-09-22). The contract was rebuilt from the IoT Connector
API definition, so its examples are now exactly the API definition's own. The earlier drop also
carried examples backfilled from the Zebra API reference site -- error replies, the reply with
no response.code, a DELETE post filter, a bulk certificate delete -- and the pages' payloads
matched those. Those examples are gone, so the payloads below have no twin to adopt. Each
reason names the scenario the contract does not carry, and says whether the payload validates
against its message; the ones that do not are there to document a reader deviation that the
page names in its caption or text.
WHAT WOULD RETIRE THEM: upstream examples for the error replies, the empty and bulk cases,
the request envelopes of the five read commands, and FIRMWARE_UPDATE progress and success;
firmware that always sends response.code; and a numeric apiVersion enum on epConnectionEvent.

waived.ctrl/control-operation.mdx:ERROR12_JSON: Code 12 reply to a STOP sent while the radio is idle. Same cause as ERROR11_JSON: no error-reply example for control_operation in the contract. The payload validates.
waived.ctrl/control-operation.mdx:SUCCESS_NOCOD: The reported success reply that omits response.code, shown under a caption saying the contract does not accept it. waived.events/heartbeat-event.mdx:INVENTORY_ONL: A heartbeat carrying only the inventory block, the case where heartbeatConfiguration.batteryStatus is false. The contract's one heartBeatEvent example carries both blocks. The payload validates against heartBeatEvent.
waived.events/heartbeat-event.mdx:MINIMAL_JSON: A heartbeat carrying only the three required fields. The contract's one heartBeatEvent example carries data, so the required-only shape has no twin. The payload validates.
waived.events/mqtt-connection-event.mdx:CTRL_CO: A CONNECTED event from a second (CTRL) endpoint, showing per-endpoint emission; the contract's two examples come from one endpoint. Like them it carries apiVersion 1.21, which fails the contract's enum of V-strings on a number field, the schema defect the page describes. Retired when that enum is corrected upstream and a CTRL example is added.

waived.mgmt/config-endpoint.mdx:DUP_JSON: Code 10 reply to a duplicate add. The contract carries only the success reply for config_endpoint. The payload validates against configEndpointResponse.

waived.mgmt/set-os.mdx:FW_PROGRESS_JSON: FIRMWARE_UPDATE progress at 87%, recorded from a reader. waived.mgmt/set-os.mdx:FW_FILE_JSON: FIRMWARE_UPDATE per-file progress at 98%, recorded from a reader; same cause as FW_PROGRESS_JSON. Its updateStatus is free text naming a file, outside the contract's enum, which is the deviation the page documents.
waived.mgmt/set-os.mdx:FW_SUCCESS_JSON: FIRMWARE_UPDATE completion at 100%, recorded from a reader. The contract ships no success-state FIRMWARE_UPDATE example; this payload validates (FW update success is an enum member). It ends the page's update walkthrough. Retired by a drop that ships a 100% example.
